analyst_view.overall: Early view: Stuttgart had their worst start under Sebastian Hoeneß but won their last two league games, including 4-2 at Leverkusen, and this comes a few days after a Champions League matchday. Frankfurt's games average close to four goals and they concede often; the brief lists Elias Baum as missing, but his one-match ban will have been served against Hoffenheim, so he should be available.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.8 goals. Frankfurt's leaky defence and Stuttgart's attack (Ermedin Demirović, Jamie Leweling, Deniz Undav) point up, but Stuttgart looked tired after their last European trip and beat Bremen only 1-0. These pull in opposite directions, so I stay with the number.

corners.text: The site expects 10.3 corners. Stuttgart attack through wing-backs and Frankfurt press high, which tends to give a steady flow of corners at both ends, but nothing suggests a big move from the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards. I lean higher: Stuttgart's game at Leverkusen had seven yellows in the first hour, and Frankfurt had Baum sent off and Adi Hütter booked in their last two games. Two pressing sides tend to produce fouls in midfield.

shots.text: The site has 30.4 shots. Stuttgart's game at Leverkusen produced 36 attempts by the 82nd minute and Hütter's Frankfurt play at high intensity, so I lean higher on volume.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.9 on target. That fits two sides with in-form finishers, Demirović for Stuttgart and Jonathan Burkardt for Frankfurt, and I see no reason to move it.
